Henry wants to bake twice as many cookies as last year. Let \( L \) be the number of cookies he baked last year. His intended amount is \( 2L \). He actually bakes 15 more than intended, so he bakes \( 2L + 15 \) cookies. After dropping 5 cookies, he has \( (2L + 15) - 5 = 2L + 10 \) cookies left. This equals 110, so:

\[
2L + 10 = 110
\]
\[
2L = 100
\]
\[
L = 50
\]

Henry baked 50 cookies last year.

Answer: 50
